the doctor dug up the records: the original survey, the territorial seal, the witness — old, afraid, but honest. a strongbox key matched, link by link. the corrupt judge's forgery claim started to look like what it was: desperation.

the doctor stood with Elena Vargas — and then the blacksmith, and the schoolteacher, and one by one half the town. 'We know Elena Vargas's word,' the sheriff said. It wasn't much. It was everything.

Thursday night they came with fire. The livery burned, and a strongbox key's copies with it — but Elena Vargas had the original where fire couldn't reach. the corrupt judge had played the last card. Friday would tell.

chapters.title: High Noon
chapters.text:
What happened next took four seconds and would be told for forty years. When the dust settled, the corrupt judge's gunmen were down — winged, not killed; Elena Vargas never shot to kill if winging would do — and the corrupt judge stood alone, empty-handed.

Friday noon. The street emptied the way streets do before a storm. Elena Vargas walked it alone — the doctor had argued, but some walks you take solo. a strongbox key was in the courthouse. This was about more than paper.

the corrupt judge's claim died that afternoon, in public, on the record. the frontier town of Hope exhaled. the doctor bought the drinks. Elena Vargas drank one, slow, tasting justice. It tasted like dust and sweet water.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.text:
the corrupt judge's rustlers hit them at the canyon — the last play of a losing hand. The fight was short and decisive: the town rode together, and together is a word the corrupt judge never understood.

Elena Vargas organized the drive: every ranch, every hand, moving the herds to the railhead themselves, cutting out the corrupt judge's middlemen. the doctor rode drag. a strongbox key — the deed — rode in Elena Vargas's breast pocket, the reason for it all.

They reached the railhead with the herds and the deed and their heads high. the frontier town of Hope was solvent. the frontier town of Hope was free. Elena Vargas looked back at the dust of the trail and felt the peculiar ache of a job done.

chapters.title: Home Range
chapters.text:
the corrupt judge was last seen heading east, smaller in the distance. the frontier town of Hope didn't gloat. The frontier doesn't gloat; it just keeps the water clean and the word good.

a strongbox key stayed in the courthouse, under glass, with the iron likeness beside it. Proof. Promise. justice rides slow but sure — carved, at the doctor's insistence, on the frame.

the frontier town of Hope threw a dance. the doctor danced every dance. The schoolteacher cried. The blacksmith forged a strongbox key's likeness in iron for the courthouse wall — 'so nobody forgets,' he said.

chapters.title: Sundown
chapters.text:
Elena Vargas rides somewhere west, where the map goes blank. There are always more valleys, more villains, more folks needing one person to stand. The frontier doesn't end. It just moves.

the doctor keeps a room ready, and the kettle on, and the news of the frontier town of Hope in letters. 'Come home when the trail allows,' every letter ends. The trail always allows, eventually.

the frontier town of Hope is still there, in the valley, under the big sky. The water runs. The cattle graze. The deed holds. Travelers ask about the iron a strongbox key in the courthouse, and the old-timers tell it true.
